name: Sikh state of Banda Singh Bahadur

predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: the province of Sirhind and its 28 parganas, 'from the Sutlej to the Yamuna', taken from the Mughal governors in 1709-1710

successors.name: Mughal Empire
successors.text: the pockets Banda still held: the Gurdas Nangal fort, where the Mughals 'broke into the starving garrison' on 7 December 1715

ledger.x: November 1709: Banda Singh Bahadur takes Samana and founds the first Sikh state.
Early 1710: Sadhaura falls to the Sikhs.
12-14 May 1710: the Sikhs win at Chappar Chiri and enter Sirhind.
December 1710: the first Battle of Lohgarh.
1711: Sirhind is out of Sikh hands.
March 1712: Banda retakes Sadhaura and Lohgarh.
1713: the Sikhs leave Lohgarh and Sadhaura.
1713: Banda builds his dera in the Jammu hills.
March 1715: Abd al-Samad Khan's army drives Banda's forces into Gurdas Nangal; the siege runs April-December ('eight months').
7 December 1715: 'the Mughals broke into the starving garrison' and captured Banda and his companions.
December 1715: the first Sikh state ends with Banda's capture; he was blinded and beheaded in Delhi on 9 June 1716.

wars.name: Banda Singh Bahadur's Sirhind campaign
wars.outcome: Samana sacked in November 1709, Sadhaura in early 1710, Sirhind taken on 12-14 May 1710 after Chappar Chiri.

wars.name: Mughal counter-offensive and the sieges of Lohgarh and Gurdas Nangal
wars.outcome: Lohgarh fell in December 1710 (first battle); Banda retook Sadhaura and Lohgarh in 1712 (second battle, March 1712), left for the Jammu hills in 1713, was besieged at Gurdas Nangal from April 1715 and captured on 7 December 1715; executed in Delhi on 9 June…

certainty.note: The page gives a province of 28 parganas 'from the Sutlej to the Yamuna' and named forts, not boundaries; the pockets after 1710 are forts with a radius.
